requirement_text.ISS-0297: 3 test failures under 16-way scripts/test_parallel.sh parallelism: 2x Letflow.EngineConcurrencyTest (Postgres connection-pool exhaustion) and 1x Mix.Tasks.Letflow.AuditIssueClosuresTest (described as 'gh CLI timeout'). Not caused by any specific branch. Pool sizing: with N=16 partitions, max_connections=100, superuser_reserved=3, headroom=10, nonpool_reserve=2 -> budget=85, pool_size=85/16=5 per partition. Affected files: test/letflow/engine_concurrency_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/letflow.audit_issue_closures_test.exs, scripts/test_parallel.sh.

pre_loaded_diagnosis.engine_concurrency_root_cause: EngineConcurrencyTest has @instance_count 100 and launches 100 concurrent Task.async processes each needing a DB connection via Letflow.DataCase (async: false, each task checks out its own connection). With pool_size=5 at N=16, the test exhausts the 5-connection pool immediately when it calls complete_all_concurrently!/2 with 100 instances. This is a pool-size-vs-test-demand mismatch: the test MUST run with pool_size >= 100 to avoid exhaustion.
pre_loaded_diagnosis.audit_closures_root_cause: AuditIssueClosuresTest calls Audit.run([]) which (1) reads ALL docs/issues/*.yaml files (hundreds, growing), (2) makes a System.cmd('gh', ...) subprocess call for each tracked+closed issue. Under 16-way parallel load the test competes for I/O and CPU for these hundreds of file reads and subprocess spawns, and may exceed ExUnit's default 60-second timeout. The test uses a fake gh.bat so no real network calls are made -- the timeout is load-induced slowness, not network delay.

fix_options.engine_concurrency: Option A (PREFERRED): Add @moduletag :high_pool_demand to engine_concurrency_test.exs and update scripts/test_parallel.sh to pass --exclude high_pool_demand when computed pool_size < @instance_count (i.e., < 100, which happens at any N >= 2 on a 100-max_connections Postgres). The test must run only when pool_size >= 100 or when the caller explicitly includes it. Option B: Reduce @instance_count to something that fits in pool_size=5, but this defeats the test's purpose (AC2 explicitly requires 100 instances to demonstrate real concurrency).
fix_options.audit_closures: Option A (PREFERRED): Add @moduletag timeout: 120_000 (2 minutes) to AuditIssueClosuresTest to prevent the timeout under load -- the test is legitimately slow when the docs/issues/ corpus is large but should not be skipped. Option B: Tag it :high_load_sensitive and exclude from 16-way runs, but this leaves the test running only in single-partition mode which defeats parallelism coverage. Option C: Speed up the test by reducing the corpus read (but the moduledoc explicitly tests the real corpus).

prior_matching_issues.similarity: Same surface symptom (pool exhaustion under N-way parallelism) but DIFFERENT root cause: ISS-0194 was all N partitions combined exhausting Postgres max_connections (N*pool_size > max_connections). ISS-0297 is a single test whose own concurrent demand (100 tasks) exceeds its partition's computed pool_size (5). ISS-0194's fix (the pool clamp formula) is in place and working correctly -- it is not recurrence.

registry_lookup.conclusion: ISS-0194 is the closest prior. Not a recurrence. ISS-0297 is a distinct class: inter-test vs intra-test resource exhaustion.

result.summary:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED for both failures:

## Failure 1 & 2: Letflow.EngineConcurrencyTest (2x failures, pool exhaustion)

Empirical evidence:
- `@instance_count 100` confirmed at test/letflow/engine_concurrency_test.exs:63
- `complete_all_concurrently!/2` (lines 225-239) calls `Enum.map(instances, fn ... -> Task.async(...) end)` and then `Task.await_many(tasks, 30_000)` -- all 100 Task.async bodies are spawned BEFORE any is awaited, so all 100 run concurrently and each checks out its own Repo connection in `:auto` sandbox mode
- pool_size at N=16 computed by scripts/test_parallel.sh: `usable_ceiling = 100 - 3 = 97`, `budget = 97 - 10 - 2 = 85`, `computed_pool = floor(85 / 16) = 5`; config/test.exs reads TEST_POOL_SIZE=5
- MISMATCH: pool_size=5 vs concurrent demand=100. When complete_all_concurrently!/2 fires, 100 tasks compete for 5 connections. The first 5 succeed; the other 95 queue on DBConnection and hit checkout timeout, causing pool exhaustion errors.
- The test REQUIRES pool_size >= 100 to run correctly (all 100 tasks must hold a connection simultaneously to demonstrate genuine row-lock isolation). Any N >= 2 on a 100-max_connections Postgres will compute pool_size <= 42, always below 100.

## Failure 3: Mix.Tasks.Letflow.AuditIssueClosuresTest (1x failure, ExUnit timeout)

Empirical evidence:
- The 'grandfathered?/1 membership -- integration via run/1 with a faked gh' describe block (lines 247+) calls `Audit.run([])` at line 334 against the REAL `docs/issues/` corpus (confirmed: moduledoc lines 42/66 state this explicitly; grep confirms `Audit.tracked_issues("docs/issues")` at line 142)
- Corpus size confirmed: `(Get-ChildItem docs/issues -Filter '*.yaml').Count` = **201 YAML files**
- The fake `gh` (a `gh.bat`/`gh` shell script) is used, so no real network calls are made -- the 'gh CLI timeout' label in the issue title is misleading. The actual mechanism is: Audit.run([]) reads all 201 YAML files, identifies tracked+closed issues, and calls `System.cmd('gh', ...)` once per closed tracked issue via the fake script
- ExUnit default test timeout is 60 seconds. Under 16-way CPU and I/O contention, processing 201 files plus subprocess spawns can exceed 60s, triggering the ExUnit timeout kill, which manifests as an apparent 'gh CLI timeout' in the failure message
- This is a load-induced timeout, not a test-isolation gap or network issue.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design: (1) Add @moduletag :high_pool_demand to Letflow.EngineConcurrencyTest and update scripts/test_parallel.sh to pass --exclude high_pool_demand when computed pool_size < 100 (i.e., at any N >= 2 on a 100-max_connections Postgres, since floor(85/2)=42 < 100); the test must run only in single-partition mode or when pool_size >= 100. (2) Add @moduletag timeout: 120_000 to Mix.Tasks.Letflow.AuditIssueClosuresTest (the grandfathered?/1 describe block or at module level) to allow 2 minutes for the 201-file real-corpus run under high parallel load.
